info.title: Thapsus-HR API
info.description: Versioned public REST API. All responses are served from the tenant's home region and are never cached at the edge.

session.name: __Host-thr_sid
session.description: Browser session (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax). Plain-HTTP local development uses the name thr_sid.

bearer.description: Scoped API key (thr_sk_…) or OAuth 2.0 access token (thr_at_…). See docs/api.md.

oauth2.description: OAuth 2.0 client credentials (RFC 6749 §4.4). Effective permissions = the client role ∩ the granted scopes.

scopes.employees:write: Allows: employees.read, employees.history, employees.create, employees.update, employees.terminate
scopes.leave:write: Allows: leave.read, absence.read, leave.record, leave.manage, leave.adjust, absence.record
scopes.time:write: Allows: time.read, rota.view, rota.manage, time.manage, time.correct, time.approve

post.summary: Sign in with email and password
Change (or set a first) password; ends your other sessions
post.description: The current password is required when one exists, except within the re-authentication window after signing in with an emailed link (ADR-0171). Setting a first password (for people invited by link or SSO) needs a recent sign-in or re-authentication.

post.summary: Prove your identity again before a sensitive change (password or authenticator code)

get.summary: Your active sessions on every device

Remove a person’s lost second factors after confirming who they are; they set up a new one at their next sign-in
post.description: Needs company-wide settings.manage, every permission the person holds, and a recent sign-in or re-authentication. You cannot reset your own factors. The person is signed out everywhere and told by email.

post.summary: Ask for a password-reset link by email (the same answer whether or not the account exists)
Set a new password with a reset link; every session ends and the person is told by email
post.description: The link is single-use and does not sign you in: sign in with the new password afterwards, and with your second factor if you have one.

post.summary: Email a person a link to set a new password (you never see or set it)
post.description: Needs company-wide settings.manage, every permission the person holds, and a recent sign-in or re-authentication; never for yourself. The link works once, for 24 hours. Their sessions end when they use it; their second factor is unchanged.
